summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee approved $10,456 for Glow SoBo holiday lighting and advanced plans for parade logistics, music festivals, and time capsule storage.
summary.summary: The Southborough Tricentennial Committee reviewed progress across multiple planned events for the town's 2027 anniversary celebration. The committee voted unanimously to approve a $10,456 expenditure for decorative holiday lighting for the winter Glow SoBo event. Members coordinated with the Recreation Department on logistics for a New Year's Day kickoff drone show and bonfire, as well as an expanded Summer Nights music festival. Updates were also presented on parade entries, above-ground time capsule photo preservation, and municipal utility pole banners.

topics.title: New Year's Day kickoff and drone show coordination
topics.summary: The committee coordinated with the recreation director on plans for the opening day of the tricentennial celebration on January 1, 2027. Planned activities include morning yoga at the Senior Center, afternoon family entertainment at Woodward School, an evening drone light show launched from St. Mark's School, and a concluding bonfire managed by the local fire department union. Members discussed potential viewing locations, traffic flow, and coordinating logistics with St. Mark's School.
key_details: Events are planned for Friday, January 1, 2027.
The drone show is targeted to start at 6:00 PM, followed immediately by the bonfire.
The fire department union has committed to sourcing materials and building the bonfire.
Woodward School is being eyed for indoor family activities prior to the drone show.
topics.outcome: Committee members will confirm space availability and written permission from St. Mark's School.

topics.title: Summer Nights 2027 music festival planning
topics.summary: The committee discussed expanding the town's traditional Summer Nights event in August 2027 into a larger music festival. Plans under review include an earlier start time around 1:00 PM, a larger stage requiring early booking deposits, additional police details, and food trucks. Organizers reported ongoing grant research to fund performers and noted that singer Storm Large expressed interest in headlining at a discounted fee.
key_details: Summer Nights 2027 is targeted for Saturday, August 21, 2027.
Stage vendors require a $2 million town liability insurance certificate and bookings up to a year in advance.
Contracts must be processed through the town administrator for official signature.
Organizers are considering Neary School fields as the primary venue, with Trottier Middle School as a backup.
topics.outcome: Organizers will meet with recreation staff to draft firm timelines and cost estimates for the September meeting.

topics.title: Volunteer recruitment and utility pole banners
topics.summary: A resident involved in local sports leagues attended to offer volunteer assistance and explore joining the committee or working groups. The committee discussed filling two vacant seats on the nine-member board and directing volunteers to subcommittees such as the parade or banner installation. The chair also reviewed progress on installing commemorative street banners on 87 utility poles across the town's four villages, which requires formal approvals from National Grid and Verizon.
key_details: The committee has two vacant seats among its nine authorized positions.
87 candidate utility poles have been inventoried across Southville, Cordaville, Fayville, and Southborough center.
National Grid guidelines restrict sponsor logos on banners to no more than 10 percent of banner fixture area.
Banners on Main Street must coordinate around existing American flag brackets mounted 9 feet high.
topics.outcome: Staff and committee members will submit pole inventory lists to utility companies and connect interested volunteers to specific tasks.

topics.title: Parade, fire muster, and time capsule updates
topics.summary: Working groups reported progress on several signature anniversary events. Updates covered parade participant recruitment, including pricing for a historic cannon firing ($500 for shots, $750 for marching) and renting an oxen team on a sled ($2,200). For the time capsule, organizers recommended shifting from underground burial to an above-ground display inside a public building to ensure photograph survival without requiring $2,000 to $4,500 in specialized preservation enclosures.
key_details: Commemorative coins have been minted for the Fireman's Muster scheduled for July 17, 2027.
The town's original handtub, the Falcon, is undergoing restoration for the muster.
A historic cannon entry proposal costs $750 for parade marching and $500 for firing demonstration rounds.
An above-ground indoor location for the time capsule is proposed to prevent photo degradation.
The History Makers initiative is scheduled to launch marketing in mid-September 2026.
topics.outcome: Working group leads will finalize entry contracts and prepare a formal time capsule placement recommendation for the Select Board.

topics.title: Glow SoBo holiday lighting contract and event scope
topics.summary: The committee evaluated the budget and scope for the Glow SoBo winter lighting celebration. Members discussed whether to keep the gathering simple with hot drinks and cookies or expand to a catered event, ultimately leaning toward a simpler format due to space constraints at the Community House. The committee formally voted to authorize $10,456 for professional exterior lighting covering Town House, library grounds, and nearby trees.
key_details: The approved lighting contract amount is $10,456.
Lighting will cover trees, Town House, and the Southborough Library properties.
The event is tentatively scheduled for Friday evening in early December.
Members considered alternative indoor venues such as Pilgrim Church hall to handle larger crowds.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 6-0 to approve $10,456 for the Glow SoBo lighting contract.
topics.why_it_matters: Authorizes over $10,000 in public celebration funds to decorate municipal buildings and kick off townwide winter festivities.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from July 15, 2026, with minor typographical corrections. Members also scheduled their next regular business meeting for mid-September before adjourning.
key_details: Meeting minutes of July 15, 2026, were approved as amended.
The next committee meeting was scheduled for September 16, 2026.

topics.title: Community outreach and regional school coordination
topics.summary: The chair reported on an informational presentation to approximately 40 members of the Dull Men's Club, where attendees proposed incorporating local railroad history into anniversary celebrations. A committee member reported initial discussions with regional school planning groups to coordinate student involvement and local history education through Algonquin Regional High School.
key_details: The chair presented the draft 2027 calendar to approximately 40 attendees at the Dull Men's Club.
Attendees suggested reaching out to local rail contacts regarding historical train commemoration.
Committee representatives are engaging Algonquin Regional High School civics and history clubs.
topics.outcome: Members will follow up with regional school contacts and local rail operators.

votes.motion: Approve $10,456 for town lighting for the Glow SoBo event.

upcoming.what: Tricentennial information table at Southborough Summer Nights
Marketing launch of the History Makers initiative
Presentation of time capsule recommendation to the Select Board
